To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Haldane coefficient decreases with decreasing pH, increases with increasing PCO2 and increases with increasing DPG.
(1) The Haldane coefficients of human blood are pH dependent, with a maximum at pH 7.4 and a minimum at pH 7, and (2) the Haldane coefficient is decreased by DPG, especially at low pH.
1) The oxygen-linked H+ binding of hemoglobin is a complex process, which involves the binding of H+ to two sites, the -NH2 groups of the α- and the β-chains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the oxygen-linked protonation of human hemoglobin in the erythrolysate.
the oxygen-linked hydrogen ion binding (OHIB) of human hemoglobin and its effect on the acid-base status of blood.
the oxygen-linked hydrogen ion binding (OLHI) of human hemoglobin and its dependence on the concentration of 2, 3-diphospho-glycerate (DP G) in the erythrocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DPG decreases the affinity of hemoglobin for oxygen by increasing the affinity of hemoglobins for protons and carbon dioxide.
DPG decreases the oxygen-linked proton affinity, but increases the oxygen-linked proton release.
the effect of DPG on the acid-base behavior of deoxy-hb is a decrease in Kz and an increase in Kc.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Haldane coefficient is determined by the oxygen-linked hydrogen ion binding, which is controlled by the terminal -NH₂ groups.

DPG decreases the oxygen-linked H+ affinity of the hemoglobin molecule, but increases the oxygen-linked HCO3- affinity, which is the main reason why DPG increases the Haldane coefficient at pH 7.5 and PCO2=3.6 torr.
DPG decreases the oxygen-linked hydrogen ion binding, but increases the acid-base binding of the terminal -NHS of the β-chain of deoxy-hb.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DPG has a strong effect on the acid-base titration curve of hemoglobin and this effect is not due to the direct binding of DPG to the protein.
the Haldane coefficient is a useful parameter in the study of hemoglobin function in vivo.
DPG decreases the oxygen-linked hydrogen ion binding in human erythrocytes, especially in the acid range.
